Gun or cartridge malfunctions

A malfunction is a failure of the gun or cartridge: a misfire, a second barrel that does not fire, or both barrels firing together (double discharge).

Safety: First, what the shooter must do: stay where you are, with the gun pointing down the range. Do not open it or touch the safety until the referee has examined it. Opening the gun or touching the safety first means the target or targets are scored zero. Do not try to take a loaded gun apart on the stand.

Why not open the gun straight away? Occasionally a cartridge fires late, a fraction of a second or longer after the trigger is pulled: a hang fire. If the gun is open or pointing sideways at that moment, that is dangerous. So in training without a referee, wait with the gun pointing safely before you open it; your instructor or the ground's rules will tell you how long.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

Per round of 25 targets. The first incident is a No Bird with a warning, and the target is repeated. From the second, the target is not repeated but scored zero.

Compak® Sporting

Per round of 25 targets. The first incident is a No Bird with a yellow card. A second of the same kind brings a red card, and targets not shot at are zero.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

Your first malfunction in the round, case by case. (1) The first shot fails: you shoot the single or the double again. If you still fired the second shot, that result counts. (2) On a single, the second shot fails: you shoot it again, and on the repeat only a hit with the second shot counts. So miss with the first shot on purpose. (3) Both barrels go off at once at a single, or at the first target of a double: No Bird, nothing is written down, and you shoot again. How each kind of double is repeated is in the rules guide (Chapter 6 · Malfunction on the second shot).

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 6 · Malfunction on the first shot

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

If your gun is repaired before the squad has finished the stand, you may shoot the stand last, with the referee's permission. If it cannot be repaired, you may switch to another gun at once, with the referee's agreement, or finish later in another squad if the jury allows it. Apart from a malfunction, you may not change your gun, choke or barrels once you are on the stand.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 7 · What happens after a gun malfunction

Compak® Sporting

Your first malfunction in the round. If both barrels fire together or the first cartridge fails, the single or double is thrown again, and the failed attempt counts for nothing. If the second cartridge fails on a single, the target is thrown again, but only the second shot can score it. So miss with the first shot on purpose. For doubles, see the rules guide (Chapter 20 · The second cartridge fails).

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 20 · Both barrels fire together or the first cartridge fails

Compak® Sporting

After a malfunction you have two minutes to get the gun working again or to replace it. As an exception, you may borrow a gun from someone outside your own squad or group, with the owner's and the referee's agreement. Without a working gun, the remaining targets are zero. Otherwise no gun, choke or barrel may be changed within a round.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 21 · Malfunction: inspection, 2 minutes, replacement gun

A rabbit is the clay that rolls along the ground. In both disciplines, if you miss it with the first shot and it then breaks on its own before your second shot, it is a No Bird. This can happen when it hits a stone. On the repeat only the second shot counts, as after a second-shot malfunction.

Tip: Check your gun and cartridges before the round, on the test stand near the clubhouse if there is one. Test shots on the shooting stand are not allowed in either discipline.

Key points

  • After a failure, stay put with the gun closed and pointing down the range; opening it before the referee's check costs the target.
  • First incident in a round: a No Bird and a warning (in Compak® Sporting, a yellow card).
  • Second incident in the same round: no repeat. In Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ the target is zero. In Compak® Sporting a second failure of the same kind brings a red card, and targets not shot at are zero.
  • Second shot fails on a single: on the repeat only a hit with the second shot counts.
  • Compak® Sporting: two minutes to repair the gun or replace it.

Did you know?

Some 'malfunctions' at the start are simply a safety catch left on. A coach can teach you to check it before you call.

Stand Talk

  • Referee Stay there, don't open the gun.

    Meaning: Referee: wait for the inspection; opening first costs the target.

  • Referee Let me see the gun.

    Meaning: The referee examines the gun or cartridge.

  • Referee Malfunction. No Bird, first warning.

    Meaning: First incident in the round: the target is repeated.

  • Referee Second malfunction this round. Zero.

    Meaning: No repeat this time; the target is lost.

  • Referee Don't move, keep the gun closed.

    Meaning: Referee: wait for the inspection after a failure.

  • Referee First malfunction. Yellow card, No Bird.

    Meaning: First incident of this type in the round; the target is thrown again.

  • Referee You have two minutes.

    Meaning: Time to repair or replace the gun.

  • Referee Only the second shot counts on this one.

    Meaning: Repeat after a second-cartridge failure: miss with the first shot on purpose.

For the interpreter
  • Pass the referee's words on at once and word for word: 'stay there, don't open the gun'. Explain the reasons only after the check.

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. Your cartridge misfires. What do you do first?

    1. Open the gun and check the cartridge
    2. Reload at once and call again
    3. Stay put, gun closed, and wait for the referee
    Answer

    Stay put, gun closed, and wait for the referee

    Opening the gun or touching the safety before the referee's check means the target is scored zero.

    Chapter 8 · After a misfire: do not open the gun

  2. In Sporting™, a second gun malfunction happens in the same round, on a single. What is the result?

    1. Zero
    2. No Bird
    3. One
    Answer

    Zero

    Only the first malfunction in a round is a No Bird; from the second, the target is scored zero.

    Chapter 6 · Second malfunction in the same round

  3. How long do you have in Compak® Sporting to repair or replace the gun?

    1. 30 seconds
    2. 2 minutes
    3. 10 minutes
    Answer

    2 minutes

    You have two minutes; without a working gun, the targets not shot are zero.

    Chapter 21 · Malfunction: inspection, 2 minutes, replacement gun
